_doc: PINNED rustup-init — the only rustup installer tools/setup/ may execute.
WHAT IT REPLACES. tools/setup/common/install-rust-wasm32.sh:32 was, until
081M24HZCYN087G0R002MT55TV:
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | \
sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain "$RUST_VERSION" --no-modify-path
the last live pipe-to-shell on the install path. `install.sh` is consumed three ways
(dev laptops, CI runners, devcontainer images, GOVERNANCE.md §24), so whatever that URL
served at that instant executed on all three, and nothing committed to this repo could
have told anyone it had changed. §13 noninterference: influence through an undeclared,
unmetered channel. Also OpenSSF Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID.
THE ORDERING IS THE PROPERTY. `curl | sh` runs the bytes as its FIRST act, so no check
performed afterwards is a check at all. src/Core.TypeScript/ace/pinned-artifact.ts
fetches, compares the SHA-256, and only then makes the file executable and runs it. A
single flipped byte refuses with NOTHING executed.
SHAPE. Same mechanism as .github/ollama-pin.json (PR #17200), extended in two ways this
dependency forced and Ollama did not: `artifacts` is a LIST, one row per platform, because
one digest cannot describe four builds; and `kind: run-installer` executes the verified
bytes instead of unpacking them, because rustup-init is an executable and not a tarball.
WHY THE ARCHIVE URL AND NOT https://sh.rustup.rs. The archive path is VERSION-ADDRESSED:
static.rust-lang.org/rustup/archive/<version>/<triple>/rustup-init is written once when
that rustup is cut and is not rewritten afterwards. sh.rustup.rs is a rolling alias that
changes with every rustup release, so pinning it would fail closed on somebody else's
schedule and would need a from-url-rolling-exceptions row. This one needs none: a new
rustup release does not touch this URL. The pin goes stale; it does not break.
FAILURE MODE: FAIL CLOSED, deliberately, and it is NOT an increase in blast radius. The
call site runs under `set -euo pipefail` and the previous `curl … | sh` aborted install.sh
on a network failure too, so the shape of a bad day is unchanged. What is refused is a
FALLBACK to the unpinned installer: a check with a bypass is not a check. If the pin
cannot be satisfied, Rust is not installed and install.sh stops with the reason named.
REFRESH (the maintenance path), when a newer rustup is wanted. Never hand-edit a digest:
1. bun src/Core.TypeScript/ace/refresh-rustup-pin.ts [--version 1.29.1]
2. commit on a branch, push, open a PR — verify-rustup-pin.yml proves it on a real
ubuntu-24.04 runner: install, prove the version, AND prove the refusal path
3. merge only after it is green
HONEST LIMIT ON DIGEST PROVENANCE, stated because the ollama pin claims something
stronger and this one cannot. That refresher cross-checks TWO independent sources. rustup
has only one distribution channel: static.rust-lang.org publishes the binary and the
`.sha256` sidecar beside it, from the same origin, so agreeing with the sidecar is one
source, not two — it detects a corrupted transfer and would not detect a compromised
origin. rust-lang/rustup's GitHub releases carry no rustup-init assets to cross-check
against (measured 2026-09-10: the API has no release for tag 1.29.1 at all). The
refresher therefore records what it actually did rather than claiming independence.
MEASURED 2026-09-10: all four sidecars agreed with the sha256 of the bytes actually
fetched, and https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup/release-stable.toml named 1.29.1.

exercisedToday: linux/x86_64 — tools/setup/linux.sh:892 on ubuntu-24.04 runners and Debian/Ubuntu hosts
linux/arm64 — the same call site on an arm64 Linux host or cluster node
declaredButNotExercisedToday: darwin/x86_64 and darwin/arm64 — macos.sh does NOT call install-rust-wasm32.sh; macOS gets rust from .mise.toml. The rows are here so a macOS invocation of the script (its docstring documents a standalone run) is pinned rather than unsupported, and their digests were measured the same way as the Linux pair. Nothing on a live path proves them today, and this note exists so nobody reads their presence as coverage.

_notPinnedHere: The Rust TOOLCHAIN version (1.99.0-beta.3) is declared once, in .mise.toml, and reaches this mechanism as `--run-arg --default-toolchain <version>` from install-rust-wasm32.sh. Copying it into this file would create a second place it lives, and a pin that disagrees with .mise.toml is worse than no pin.
The toolchain bytes themselves. rustup verifies its own downloads against the Rust release signing keys; this pin covers the installer that bootstraps that trust, not everything downstream of it.
